additional_info.subject: RE: Why DPA change happens? CRM:00314000164
additional_info.body:
Good evening Benjamin,
I am reaching out regarding this old case
ID0400192.
I took over this ticket from my colleague Joao, as the ticket was missing an explanation on DPA behavior in a specific case.
We finally got an explanation from R&D in regards of the example from you provided.
To summarize: the scenario was a case when
Vehicle A is charging at connector 2 with 280kW @ 67% SOC, Vehicle B gets plug in with SOC 76% at connector 1. Charger allocate converters from DC3 and DC4 to the second EV reaching, not respecting FIFO configuration. Vehicle B is charging with less power then Vehicle A before DPA reduce the power delivery.
This scenario as described in the "not ideal" example above can happen when two EV are charging both with higher SOC levels.  The charger aggressively de-allocate the converter groups from 1st EV and provides it to second EV and it is not able to get the lost converter groups back as they are now in use by 2nd EV.
In SiD FW v6.0.3 / SiD v7.0.x, there is DPA FIFO-1 algorithm which depends on SOC levels + EV target current levels for estimation, also the timeouts are missing for de-allocation.
The improvements for handling such cases are in upcoming SiD v8.0.x with DPA FIFO-2 algorithm.
If you have any further question, feel free to reply to this email, otherwise I will close the ticket.
With kind regards,
